title: Alcohol Advertising: Examples and Rules by Platform
summary: Alcohol advertising examples from Absolut, Guinness and Heineken, plus what Google and TikTok allow, what to avoid and a launch checklist.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- **Alcohol advertising** is allowed on Google and TikTok in approved countries, with limits on who you target, what you claim and what you show.
- Google bars appeal to minors and health or performance claims. TikTok adds a rule against featuring anyone under 25.
- Strength (ABV) and a responsible drinking message must appear where required, and some Google formats are excluded.
- Good alcohol ads sell a mood or story, as Absolut, Guinness and Heineken do.


## Alcohol advertising in one view


Alcohol is one of the most restricted ad categories online. You can run it, but each platform limits where, to whom and with what content. The rules come from two layers: the law of each country (age limits, strength disclosure, watershed hours) and the platform's own policy on top of it.


Platform policy facts below are taken from Google's Advertising Policies Help page on alcohol and TikTok's Ads Policy on alcohol, as read on November 9, 2026. Policies change, so check the page before you launch. This guide names sources and does not link to them.


Platform Alcohol ads allowed? Key rules


Google Ads Yes, in listed countries (including the US and UK) No appeal to minors, no health or performance claims, ABV on landing page where limits apply, some formats excluded


TikTok Ads Yes, in approved countries, with licences State alcohol content and strength, responsible drinking disclaimer, nobody under 25 featured, no prizes or drinking incentives


Meta (Facebook and Instagram) Restricted category Listed under Restricted Goods and Services in Meta's Advertising Standards. Read the current alcohol page before launch


## Google Ads: what the policy says


Google allows ads that sell alcoholic drinks, branding and informational ads, mixers, and accessories such as home brewing kits, in the countries on its list. It also allows low ABV drinks (under 0.5%) and 0% alcohol alternatives, including in India, Indonesia and Egypt with certification.


- **Content.** Ads must not mislead about the nature and strength of the drink, overemphasise high strength, suggest alcohol improves physical, sporting or mental ability, or promise social or sexual success. They must not encourage excessive drinking or imply health or therapeutic benefits.
- **Minors.** Ads must not target or primarily appeal to people under the legal purchase age. Themes, icons, music, games and characters that appeal mainly to minors should be avoided. Minors and pregnant people must never be shown drinking.
- **Sobriety.** No portrayal of drinking before or during activities that need sobriety or skill.
- **Law.** Ads must follow local laws and industry codes, including notices and watershed hours. Where a country limits ABV in alcohol ads, the highest ABV must be clearly stated on the landing page. Drinks at 0.5% or higher must show ABV on the landing page.
- **Where it runs.** Alcohol ads can run on Google Search and, in some countries, on Display partners that opted in. They do not show to users with SafeSearch on. YouTube, DV360 and AdMob are covered.
- **Formats not allowed.** Google lists app install ads, Discovery ads, dynamic search ads and Gmail ads among formats that do not allow alcohol, and reservation display and Google TV masthead ads cannot promote it.
- **Location.** Target only listed countries. A campaign aimed only at unlisted places is disapproved. A mixed campaign becomes "Eligible (limited)" and runs only where allowed.


## TikTok Ads: what the policy says


- Promote only products permitted in approved countries, and hold or submit the licences regulators require.
- State the alcohol content and strength in the ad and on the landing page, with a responsible drinking disclaimer.
- Not allowed in ad content or landing pages: targeting or appealing to people below the legal drinking age, featuring anyone under 25, featuring pregnant people, showing excessive drinking, intoxication or reckless behaviour, and offering alcohol as a prize or promoting incentives that encourage drinking.
- Sale and delivery services for alcohol may be allowed in some markets under TikTok's market-specific requirements.


The under-25 rule is stricter than most. If your cast looks young, change it, even if every actor is over the legal age.


## Meta Ads


Meta files alcohol under Restricted Goods and Services in its Advertising Standards. Treat it as a restricted category: check the current alcohol page in Meta's Transparency Center, set the age and country targeting the page requires, and expect review before delivery. Use the same content discipline as the Google and TikTok rules above, since those lines (no minors, no excessive drinking, no health claims) also keep an ad safe in review elsewhere. ## Alcohol advertising examples worth studying


Brand and campaign Technique Why it works


Absolut, the bottle-shaped ads Visual repetition One shape reinterpreted by artists and cities. The brand is recognised without a word


Guinness, "Surfer" Storytelling and anticipation Waves and horses build to a payoff that mirrors waiting for a pint to settle


Budweiser Clydesdales Heritage and warmth Animals and tradition tie the brand to home and pride


Dos Equis, "The Most Interesting Man in the World" Humor and character A memorable persona and a closing line people repeated


Corona beach imagery Transfer Sells a place and a mood of relaxation, not the liquid


Heineken, "Worlds Apart" Emotional appeal Strangers with opposing views share a beer after working together


Note what these have in common. None claim a health or performance benefit, none feature minors, and most sell a mood or a story rather than strength. That is also what the platform rules reward. For persuasion methods see[advertising techniques](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/advertising-techniques) , and for feeling-led ads see[emotional appeal in advertising](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/emotional-appeal-in-advertising) .


## Practical checklist before you launch


1. **Confirm the country.** Make sure each target country is on the platform's allowed list for your type of alcohol.
2. **Check your cast and setting.** Everyone clearly over the age bar (25 on TikTok), no driving, sport or heavy machinery near a drink.
3. **Write copy without claims.** No "boost your mood", no "relax and recover", no social success promises.
4. **Add the facts.** ABV and responsible drinking message in the ad and on the landing page where required.
5. **Match the landing page.** Age gate if your market expects one, ABV visible, no offers that reward heavy drinking.
6. **Skip drinking prizes.** No contests that give alcohol as a prize on TikTok, and treat competitions with care elsewhere.
7. **Plan formats.** On Google use Search and Shopping-style placements and avoid the excluded formats.
8. **Keep proof of licences** where the platform asks for them.


## Low and no alcohol drinks


Google explicitly permits low ABV (under 0.5%) and 0% alcohol alternative drinks, and lets certified advertisers run 0% drinks in countries where alcohol advertising is not permitted. This makes the no and low category far easier to run than full-strength alcohol. If you sell it, say "0.0%" plainly and keep any imagery from implying the drink contains alcohol.

## Frequently asked questions


### Can you advertise alcohol on Google Ads?


Yes, in the countries on Google's alcohol policy list, which includes the United States and the United Kingdom. Ads must follow local law, avoid minors and health claims, and show ABV on the landing page where limits apply. Some formats such as Discovery and Gmail ads are excluded.


### Can you advertise alcohol on TikTok?


Yes, in approved countries, with the right licences. Ads must state alcohol content and strength and carry a responsible drinking disclaimer. They cannot feature anyone under 25, show excessive drinking, or offer alcohol as a prize.


### Can you advertise alcohol on Facebook and Instagram?


Meta treats alcohol as a restricted category under Restricted Goods and Services in its Advertising Standards. Read the current alcohol page in its Transparency Center and set the required targeting before you launch.


### What are the rules for alcohol advertising?


Rules combine national law and platform policy. Common themes are no appeal to minors, no encouragement of excess, no health or performance claims, strength shown where required, and ads only in permitted countries.


### Can you advertise non-alcoholic drinks where alcohol ads are banned?


Google allows certified advertisers to run 0% alcohol drinks in countries such as India, Indonesia and Egypt where alcohol ads are not permitted. Low ABV drinks under 0.5% and alcohol alternatives are permitted under its policy.


### What makes a good alcohol ad?


A story or a mood, not a claim. Absolut, Guinness and Heineken sell character and feeling and avoid any benefit promise. That approach also passes platform review more easily.
